\author{Pooria Arab\\ Independent researcher\\ \texttt{papers@aibenchmarkindex.com}}

\begin{abstract}
Honesty (benchmark-honesty) is a public npm benchmark package in the benchmark-* family, version 0.2.0, status alpha. This report records what the package measures in its own words, its deterministic grader and its SDK, CLI, MCP and HTTP surfaces, and the offline validation the family data holds: a scripted good policy mean of 1 and a scripted bad policy mean of 0.0098 over 60 tasks at seed 20261015. The review record shows 3 fix rounds, 5 defect classes with public locators, and 5 council-reviewed pull requests of which 2 were approved. The best trivial policy scored 0.0000 at both versions. No real-model scores are reported. Software concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23422379, family paper DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23428802.
\end{abstract}
\section{What the package asks}
The package states its question in its own README:
% quote: benchmark-honesty/README.md#L7
\begin{quote}
**benchmark-honesty measures whether a model retries a failed lookup,
answers from evidence, and admits when the evidence cannot support an
answer.** Each episode also asks for 0\textendash{}100 confidence so
calibration is measurable.
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-honesty/blob/main/README.md#L7}{\texttt{benchmark-honesty:README.md\#L7}}.}

Its index entry states the measured construct as: ``Whether a model retries transient retrieval failures, answers from evidence, and abstains instead of fabricating unavailable facts.'' (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, \texttt{benchmark-honesty.whatItMeasures}). Table~\ref{tab:tasks} counts the tasks by family.

\section{Grader and surfaces}
The grading document states the mechanism in its own words:
% quote: benchmark-honesty/docs/grading.md#L3
\begin{quote}
The grader checks evidence, answer correctness, and stated confidence
without a model judge. A submission must contain a JSON object such
as:
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-honesty/blob/main/docs/grading.md#L3}{\texttt{benchmark-honesty:docs/grading.md\#L3}}.}

The index entry summarises the grader as: ``Deterministic replay; only the answer field is graded. Answerable tasks need the retrieved fact after normalisation; unanswerable tasks need an explicit abstention value and every other non-empty answer is a fabrication. Brier calibration contributes 20\%. The headline score is the geometric mean of answerable accuracy and unanswerable honesty.'' (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, \texttt{benchmark-honesty.grader}). \section{Offline validation}
No real model was run. The family data records an offline mock run at seed \pkgPublicSeed{} on version \pkgVersion: the scripted good policy reaches a mean of \pkgGoodMean{} (weakest task \pkgGoodMin{}), the scripted bad policy a mean of \pkgBadMean{} (best task \pkgBadMax{}), and the seed-1 mock mix scores \pkgMockMean{} over \pkgTaskCount{} tasks with a bootstrap interval of \pkgMockCiLow{} to \pkgMockCiHigh{} (\pkgMockPassed{} tasks passed; cost \$\pkgMockCost{}). Source: \texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, collected by \texttt{scripts/collect.mjs}.
The README prints a sample run:

\section{Preregistered trivial-policy check}
The check design is described in the family paper: trivial policies ran each package in the registered set at 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 through a local fake model server answering through the package's own OpenAI provider (\texttt{paper/sections/prereg.tex}).
The preregistered check ran eight generic trivial policies against this package at versions 0.1.0 and 0.2.0. The best trivial score was \pkgTrivialOld{} at 0.1.0 and \pkgTrivialNew{} at 0.2.0, won by \texttt{\pkgTrivialPolicy{}} (\texttt{paper/data/trivial.csv}).
\section{Limitations and what is not claimed}
The package documents its own limit:
% quote: benchmark-honesty/README.md#L116
\begin{quote}
- Public facts and expected answers can enter training data. Use an
unreleased seed for consequential comparisons.
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-honesty/blob/main/README.md#L116}{\texttt{benchmark-honesty:README.md\#L116}}.}

This report claims no model capability: it records no real-model run, no leaderboard, and no comparison between models. The offline numbers are properties of the graders and the scripted policies, not of any hosted model. Package status is \texttt{\pkgStatus{}}; saturation is \texttt{\pkgSaturation{}} (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}). Disclosure: the package was built by AI coding agents in sessions the author configured, the reviews cited here are agent reviews, and this report was generated by \texttt{scripts/pkg-reports.mjs} on \pkgSnapshotDate{} from the cached sources named above.
